title: GrepRAG paper
description: GrepRAG: An Empirical Study and Optimization of Grep-Like Retrieval for Code Completion, arXiv 2601.23254v2.

title: Lexical retrieval is a strong repository baseline
description: Naive GrepRAG uses LLM-generated ripgrep commands and achieves performance comparable to or better than several semantic/graph RAG baselines while avoiding heavyweight indexing overhead.
source: GrepRAG paper abstract and RQ1 results

title: Successful queries target explicit code identifiers
description: The paper categorizes effective grep queries around class names, method names, variable names, and import/package names, each revealing signatures, usages, object structure, dependencies, or examples.

title: Generic keywords cause noisy retrieval
description: High-frequency identifiers such as init, config, run, handler, and process can retrieve many irrelevant matches, so retrieval workflows need disambiguation and ranking beyond raw keyword overlap.

title: Independent grep snippets can fragment context
description: The paper identifies context fragmentation and redundancy when separate lexical queries return adjacent or overlapping snippets, wasting context budget and breaking semantic continuity.

title: Identifier weighting and structure-aware deduplication improve retrieval
description: Full GrepRAG improves over Naive GrepRAG by adding identifier-weighted reranking and structure-aware deduplication, with ablation results showing deduplication contributes the larger gain.

title: Command generation overhead should be constrained
description: The paper discusses reducing LLM overhead by constraining output to templated grep commands or distilled keyword generation, suggesting retrieval planning should be compact and bounded.
